If you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and will not close off your poverty.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ali, who said: "Tilth is of two kinds: the tilth of this world, which is wealth and children, and the tilth of the Hereafter, which is the lasting good deeds."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Tawus, from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about His saying ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The near of kin of the family of Muhammad." Ibn Abbas said: "I hasten to note that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the sake of my kinship, and that you protect the kinship that is between me and you."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: "People argued much about us concerning this verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾. So we wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about it, and he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the central link of lineage in Quraysh; there was no clan among its clans except that he had kinship with it. So Allah said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, that you love me because of your kinship with me, and that you protect me through it.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had kinship with all of Quraysh. When they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, he said: 'O people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then protect my kinship with you, and let no one other than you among the Arabs be more worthy of guarding and supporting me than you.'" Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, through another route, something similar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Ansar said: 'We did this and we did that,' and it seemed they were boasting. Al-Abbas said: 'We have superiority over you.' This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he came to them in their gatherings and said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humbled, and did Allah not honor you?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Will you not answer?' They said: 'What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Will you not say: Did your people not expel you, and we sheltered you? Did they not deny you, and we affirmed you? Did they not forsake you, and we supported you?' He kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said: 'Our wealth and what is in our hands belong to Allah and His Messenger.' Then this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾." In its chain is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who is weak. The more likely view is that the verse is Meccan, not Medinan. We have already pointed out at the beginning of the surah the view of those who said that this verse and what follows it are Medinan, and this is their evidence.

Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami narrated through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, that is: you protect me concerning my family and love them because of me."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us?' He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists would love the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed, saying to them, O Muhammad: ﴿I do not ask you for it﴾, meaning, for what I call you to, ﴿any reward of a worldly kind﴾, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, except that you protect me concerning my kinship with you. When he migrated to Medina, he wanted to join him with his brothers among the prophets, so he said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47], meaning: His reward and His honor in the Hereafter, as Noah said: ﴿I ask you for no reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and as Hud, Salih, and Shu'ayb said. They did not make an exception for a reward as the Prophet (ﷺ) did, so it was rejected from them. And this verse is abrogated."

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse: "Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience."

This is the summary of what has been transmitted from the scholar of the Ummah, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the interpretation of this verse.

The first meaning is the one that is authentically reported from him, and it was narrated from him by a great number of his students and those after them. The report of abrogation transmitted from him does not contradict this. There is no obstacle to the Qur'an having been revealed in Mecca while the Quraysh disbelievers loved him because of the kinship between him and them, and protected him through it. Then that was abrogated, and this exception was removed from its origin, as indicated by what we have mentioned that shows he did not ask any reward at all for conveying the message. The view transmitted about interpreting it as referring to the family of Muhammad (ﷺ) is not strong enough to oppose the many reliable routes authentically reported from Ibn Abbas. Allah has indeed made the family of Muhammad independent of this through their noble virtues and beautiful qualities, and we have explained some of that when commenting on His saying: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Just as this view cannot withstand opposition, so too the report from him that the meaning of "affection in the near of kin" is that they love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience is not strong enough. However, what strengthens this view is that it is a tafsir traced back (marfu') to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Its chain in Ahmad's Musnad is as follows: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said it, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Qaza'ah, with this same chain.

Ibn al-Mubarak, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated.

al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu Hani' al-Khawlani, who said: "I heard Umar ibn Huraith and others saying: This verse was only revealed concerning the Companions of the Suffah: ﴿Had Allah expanded provision for His servants, they would have transgressed upon the earth﴾. That is because they said: 'If only we had...', and they wished for the world."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ali something similar.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 42, verses 19–28 (part 1 of 2):

His words, ﴿Allah is Subtly Kind (latif) to His servants﴾: that is, He is greatly kind to them and extremely compassionate toward them.

Muqatil said: "Latif toward the righteous and the wicked, in that He does not kill them with hunger because of their sins." Ikrimah said: "Bārr (kind) toward them." Al-Suddi said: "Rafiq (gentle) toward them." It was also said: "Ḥafiyy (solicitous) toward them." Al-Qurtubi said: "Latif toward them in the presentation (of deeds) and in the reckoning," and other things have been said.

The meaning is that He extends His kindness to His servants in all their affairs, and among that is the provision (rizq) by which they live in this world. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾ from among them, however He wills. So He widens it for one and restricts it for another. ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, the Mighty in power, the Overpowering, the Capable, the Dominant who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth (ḥarth) of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾. Ḥarth in the language means earning. It is said: "He tills (yaḥruthu) for his dependants," and "yaḥtarith," meaning he earns. From this, a man is named Ḥārith. The original meaning of ḥarth is casting seed into the earth, and it was then applied, by way of metaphor (istiʿārah), to the fruits and benefits of deeds. The meaning is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of the Hereafter, Allah multiplies that for him, a good deed being rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times over.

It was also said: its meaning is that He increases his success, his help, and the facilitation of the paths of good for him. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it﴾, that is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of this world, which is its enjoyment, and what Allah provides His servants from it, We give him from it what Our will decrees and what is apportioned to him in Our decree.

Qatadah said: the meaning of ﴿We give him from it﴾ is: We ordain for him what has been apportioned to him, as in His words, ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18]. Qatadah also said: Allah gives, out of the intention of the Hereafter, whatever of worldly affairs He wills, but He gives out of the intention of this world only the world. Al-Qushayri said: the apparent meaning is that the verse concerns the disbeliever, but this is a specification without a specifier (takhsīs bi-ghayr mukhassis).

Then He, glorified be He, explained that this one who intends the world by his deeds has no share in the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And he has no share in the Hereafter﴾, because he did not work for the Hereafter, so there is no share for him in it. The interpretation of this verse has already been given in Surah al-Isra'.

﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah did not permit?﴾ When He, glorified be He, had explained the principle regarding the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, He followed it with an explanation of the great sin that necessitates the Fire. The hamzah is for the interrogation of affirmation and reproach. The pronoun in "shara'ū" refers to the partners, and the pronoun in "lahum" refers to the disbelievers, though it was also said the reverse, and the first is preferred.

The meaning of ﴿what Allah did not permit﴾ is what He did not permit of polytheism and sins. ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, which is the delay of their punishment, as in His words, ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿it would have been judged between them﴾ in this world, and they would have been hastened to punishment. The pronoun in "baynahum" refers either to the believers and the polytheists, or to the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers, for them is a painful punishment﴾, that is, the polytheists and the deniers, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

The majority read "wa-inna al-ẓālimīna" with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf, beginning a new clause). Muslim, al-A'raj and Ibn Hurmuz read it with a fatḥah on it, as a conjunction over "kalimat al-faṣl" (the decisive word).

﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned﴾, that is: frightened and apprehensive of the evil deeds they earned, and that fear and apprehension will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And it will befall them﴾: the pronoun refers to "what they earned" with an elided noun in the construction, as al-Zajjaj said, that is: the recompense of what they earned will befall them and descend upon them without doubt, whether they feared it or not. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

Having mentioned the state of the wrongdoers, He mentioned the state of the believers, saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, in the meadows of the gardens﴾. Rawḍāt is the plural of rawḍah.

Abu Hayyan said: the common dialect is to pronounce the waw with a sukūn, while the dialect of Hudhayl pronounces it with a fatḥah. The rawḍah is a pleasant place abundant in greenery, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surah al-Rum. The rawḍah of Paradise is the finest of its dwellings, just as in this world it is the best of places. ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾ of kinds of blessings and types of delights. The governing element of "ʿinda rabbihim" is "yashāʾūna," or the governing element of "rawḍāt al-jannāt" is the stability (al-istiqrār). The indication by His words, "that" (dhālika), refers to what was mentioned before for the believers, and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it, which is ﴿It is the great bounty﴾, that is, one that cannot be described and that minds cannot reach in knowing its reality.

The indication by His words, ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants﴾, refers to the great bounty, that is: He gives them the good news of it.

Then He described the servants by His words, ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. These are the ones who combine faith and action in accordance with what Allah commanded and abstaining from what He forbade, and they are the ones given that good news.

The majority read "yubashshiru" with shaddah, from "bashsharа". Mujahid and Humayd ibn Qays read it with a ḍammah on the initial letter, a sukūn on the bā', and a kasrah on the shīn, from "abshara". Some of the Seven read it with a fatḥah on the initial letter and a ḍammah on the shīn. The explanation of the readings for this word has already passed.

Then, when He, glorified be He, mentioned what He informed His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, of these noble rulings contained in His Book, He commanded him to inform them that he does not ask them for any reward for this conveyance. So He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is: say, O Muhammad: I do not seek from you any payment or benefit for conveying the message, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. This exception may be connected (muttaṣil), meaning: except that you love me for my kinship among you, or love the people of my kin. It may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).

Al-Zajjaj said: "illā al-mawaddah" is an exception that is not from the first, meaning: except that you love me for my kinship, so that you protect me. The address is to the Quraysh, and this is the view of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik and al-Sha'bi. The meaning, on the disconnected reading, is: I do not ask you any reward at all, but I ask you for affection in the kinship that is between me and you. Respect me in it and do not hasten against me; leave me and the people. This was also the view of Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others, and it is the established view from Ibn ʿAbbas, as will come.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: they are the family of Muhammad. What those who hold this view cited as evidence will come.

Al-Hasan and others said: the meaning of the verse is: except seeking the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and drawing near to Him through obedience to Him.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Dahhak: this verse is abrogated (mansukh, superseded by a later ruling) and was revealed only in Mecca, when the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace. So Allah commanded them to show love to him. When he migrated, the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, and Allah then revealed to him: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and He revealed to him: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47].

What will make the reward clear and the meaning of the verse manifest will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him therein good﴾. The root of qarf is earning. It is said: "Fulan yaqrifu li-ʿiyālihi," meaning he earns for his dependants, and iqtirāf is earning, derived from their saying "rajul qirfah," when a man is cunning.

The meaning is: whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him this good deed in goodness by multiplying its reward.

Muqatil said: the meaning is: whoever earns a single good deed, We increase for him therein goodness, multiplying the single one tenfold or more.

It was also said: what is meant by this good deed is the affection for the near of kin, but applying it to the general sense is preferred, and the affection for the near of kin enters under it as a primary inclusion. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾, that is: abundantly forgiving to the sinners, and abundantly appreciative to the obedient.

Qatadah said: "Forgiving of sins, Appreciative of good deeds." al-Suddi said: "Forgiving of the sins of the family of Muhammad."

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ Am here is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿah) one, meaning: rather, do they say that Muhammad has fabricated a lie against Allah, by claiming prophethood? The denial is for rebuke. The meaning of fabricating a lie is inventing it.

Then He, glorified be He, answered their saying, saying: ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal over your heart﴾, that is: if he had fabricated a lie against Allah, He would have willed that it not come forth from him, and would have sealed upon his heart so that nothing of what he lied about would occur to his mind, as you claim.

Qatadah said: "He would seal over your heart, so He would make you forget the Qur'an." So He informed them that if he had fabricated against Him, He would have done to him what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said: "If He wills, He would bind your heart with patience regarding their harm, so that no hardship from their words enters your heart." It was also said: the address is to him, and what is meant is the disbelievers, that is: if He wills, He would seal the hearts of the disbelievers and hasten punishment upon them. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

It was also said: the meaning is: if your self had suggested to you to fabricate a lie against Allah, He would have sealed your heart, for no one dares to lie except one whose heart is sealed. The first view is preferred.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf) that confirms what precedes it of the denial of fabrication. Ibn al-Anbari said: "yakhtim ʿalā qalbika" is a complete clause, meaning that what follows is a new sentence. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in it, that is: and Allah erases falsehood. Al-Zajjaj said: "Am yaqūlūna iftarā ʿalā Allāhi kadhiban" is a complete clause.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are an argument against those who deny what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought, meaning: if what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought were false, He would have erased it, as His custom has been with fabricators. ﴿And establishes the truth through His words﴾, that is, Islam, and He makes it clear by His words, that is, by what He revealed of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, aware of what is in the hearts of the servants. The waw in "wa-yamḥu" was dropped in some copies of the Qur'an, as al-Kisa'i related.

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, that is: He accepts from the sinners among His servants their repentance to Him for the sins they committed and the evil deeds they earned. Repentance (tawbah) is regret over disobedience, with resolve not to return to it. It was also said: He accepts repentance from His friends and the people of His obedience. The first is preferred, for repentance is accepted from all servants, Muslim and disbeliever alike (p-1328), when it is sound, proceeding from sincerity of intention and sound resolve. ﴿And pardons evil deeds﴾ in general, for whoever repents of his evil deed. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾, of good and evil, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves.

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read "tafʿalūna" with the second person (taʾ) as address. The rest read it with the third person (yāʾ) as narration. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred the second reading, because this verb falls between two statements.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, He responds to them﴾. The relative pronoun is in the accusative position: Allah responds to those who believed and gives them what they asked of Him. It is said: "ajāba" and "istajāba" have the same meaning.

It was said: the meaning is that He accepts the worship of the sincere. It was also said that the implied sense is: "wa-yastajību lahum," so the lām was dropped, as it was dropped in His words, ﴿And when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3], meaning "kālū lahum" (they measured for them). It was also said that the relative pronoun is in the nominative position, meaning: they respond to their Lord when He calls them, as in His words, ﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of ﴿And those who believe respond﴾ is that those who believe seek a response; this is the true sense of the form istafʿala, so "alladhīna" is in the nominative position. The first is preferred.

﴿And He increases them from His bounty﴾, that is: He increases them beyond what they asked of Him, or beyond the reward they deserve, as a favour from Him. It was also said: He will grant them intercession for their brethren.

﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. This is for the disbelievers, in contrast to what He mentioned for the believers before it.

﴿And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would surely transgress in the earth﴾, that is: if Allah were to widen their provision, they would transgress in the earth, disobeying in it, being insolent toward the blessing, becoming arrogant, and seeking what is not theirs to seek. It was also said: the meaning is that if He made them equal in provision, some of them would not submit to others, and the crafts would cease. The first is preferred.

The apparent meaning is that it covers all kinds of provision. It has also been said that it refers specifically to rain. ﴿But He sends down in due measure what He wills.﴾ That is, He sends down provision to His servants in a measure according to His will and what His perfect wisdom requires. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing﴾ of their conditions, and sees what is good for them, whether in expanding or restricting provision. So He decrees for each one of them what suits him and restrains him from corruption through transgression on the earth.

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾ that is, the rain, which is the most beneficial kind of provision, the most widely useful, and the most productive of good. ﴿after they have despaired﴾ that is, after they have lost hope of it. Through this sending down of rain after despair, they will recognize the measure of His mercy toward them, and they will thank Him as thanks is due. ﴿And He is the Protecting Friend﴾ of His righteous servants, by doing good to them, bringing them benefits, and warding off harm from them, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, who deserves praise from them for His favors, both particular and general.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, that he said: "The life of the Hereafter." ﴿We will increase him in his tilth. And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "Whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter, Allah will not give him any share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will gain nothing from the world beyond provision that has already been finished and allotted to him."

Ahmad and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Hibban narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give good news to this Ummah of elevation, high standing, victory, and establishment in the land, so long as they do not seek the world through the deeds of the Hereafter. Whoever among them does the deeds of the Hereafter for the sake of this world, he will have no share in the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse, and then said: 'Allah says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your heart with richness and close off your poverty. If you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and will not close off your poverty.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ali, who said: "Tilth is of two kinds: the tilth of this world, which is wealth and children, and the tilth of the Hereafter, which is the lasting good deeds."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Tawus, from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about His saying ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The near of kin of the family of Muhammad." Ibn Abbas said: "I hasten to note that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the sake of my kinship, and that you protect the kinship that is between me and you."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: "People argued much about us concerning this verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾. So we wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about it, and he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the central link of lineage in Quraysh; there was no clan among its clans except that he had kinship with it. So Allah said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, that you love me because of your kinship with me, and that you protect me through it.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had kinship with all of Quraysh. When they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, he said: 'O people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then protect my kinship with you, and let no one other than you among the Arabs be more worthy of guarding and supporting me than you.'" Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, through another route, something similar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Ansar said: 'We did this and we did that,' and it seemed they were boasting. Al-Abbas said: 'We have superiority over you.' This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he came to them in their gatherings and said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humbled, and did Allah not honor you?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Will you not answer?' They said: 'What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Will you not say: Did your people not expel you, and we sheltered you? Did they not deny you, and we affirmed you? Did they not forsake you, and we supported you?' He kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said: 'Our wealth and what is in our hands belong to Allah and His Messenger.' Then this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾." In its chain is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who is weak. The more likely view is that the verse is Meccan, not Medinan. We have already pointed out at the beginning of the surah the view of those who said that this verse and what follows it are Medinan, and this is their evidence.

Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami narrated through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, that is: you protect me concerning my family and love them because of me."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us?' He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists would love the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed, saying to them, O Muhammad: ﴿I do not ask you for it﴾, meaning, for what I call you to, ﴿any reward of a worldly kind﴾, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, except that you protect me concerning my kinship with you. When he migrated to Medina, he wanted to join him with his brothers among the prophets, so he said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47], meaning: His reward and His honor in the Hereafter, as Noah said: ﴿I ask you for no reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and as Hud, Salih, and Shu'ayb said. They did not make an exception for a reward as the Prophet (ﷺ) did, so it was rejected from them. And this verse is abrogated."

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse: "Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience."

This is the summary of what has been transmitted from the scholar of the Ummah, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the interpretation of this verse.

The first meaning is the one that is authentically reported from him, and it was narrated from him by a great number of his students and those after them. The report of abrogation transmitted from him does not contradict this. There is no obstacle to the Qur'an having been revealed in Mecca while the Quraysh disbelievers loved him because of the kinship between him and them, and protected him through it. Then that was abrogated, and this exception was removed from its origin, as indicated by what we have mentioned that shows he did not ask any reward at all for conveying the message. The view transmitted about interpreting it as referring to the family of Muhammad (ﷺ) is not strong enough to oppose the many reliable routes authentically reported from Ibn Abbas. Allah has indeed made the family of Muhammad independent of this through their noble virtues and beautiful qualities, and we have explained some of that when commenting on His saying: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Just as this view cannot withstand opposition, so too the report from him that the meaning of "affection in the near of kin" is that they love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience is not strong enough. However, what strengthens this view is that it is a tafsir traced back (marfu') to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Its chain in Ahmad's Musnad is as follows: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said it, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Qaza'ah, with this same chain.

Ibn al-Mubarak, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated.

al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu Hani' al-Khawlani, who said: "I heard Umar ibn Huraith and others saying: This verse was only revealed concerning the Companions of the Suffah: ﴿Had Allah expanded provision for His servants, they would have transgressed upon the earth﴾. That is because they said: 'If only we had...', and they wished for the world."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ali something similar.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 42, verses 19–28 (part 1 of 2):

His words, ﴿Allah is Subtly Kind (latif) to His servants﴾: that is, He is greatly kind to them and extremely compassionate toward them.

Muqatil said: "Latif toward the righteous and the wicked, in that He does not kill them with hunger because of their sins." Ikrimah said: "Bārr (kind) toward them." Al-Suddi said: "Rafiq (gentle) toward them." It was also said: "Ḥafiyy (solicitous) toward them." Al-Qurtubi said: "Latif toward them in the presentation (of deeds) and in the reckoning," and other things have been said.

The meaning is that He extends His kindness to His servants in all their affairs, and among that is the provision (rizq) by which they live in this world. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾ from among them, however He wills. So He widens it for one and restricts it for another. ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, the Mighty in power, the Overpowering, the Capable, the Dominant who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth (ḥarth) of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾. Ḥarth in the language means earning. It is said: "He tills (yaḥruthu) for his dependants," and "yaḥtarith," meaning he earns. From this, a man is named Ḥārith. The original meaning of ḥarth is casting seed into the earth, and it was then applied, by way of metaphor (istiʿārah), to the fruits and benefits of deeds. The meaning is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of the Hereafter, Allah multiplies that for him, a good deed being rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times over.

It was also said: its meaning is that He increases his success, his help, and the facilitation of the paths of good for him. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it﴾, that is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of this world, which is its enjoyment, and what Allah provides His servants from it, We give him from it what Our will decrees and what is apportioned to him in Our decree.

Qatadah said: the meaning of ﴿We give him from it﴾ is: We ordain for him what has been apportioned to him, as in His words, ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18]. Qatadah also said: Allah gives, out of the intention of the Hereafter, whatever of worldly affairs He wills, but He gives out of the intention of this world only the world. Al-Qushayri said: the apparent meaning is that the verse concerns the disbeliever, but this is a specification without a specifier (takhsīs bi-ghayr mukhassis).

Then He, glorified be He, explained that this one who intends the world by his deeds has no share in the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And he has no share in the Hereafter﴾, because he did not work for the Hereafter, so there is no share for him in it. The interpretation of this verse has already been given in Surah al-Isra'.

﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah did not permit?﴾ When He, glorified be He, had explained the principle regarding the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, He followed it with an explanation of the great sin that necessitates the Fire. The hamzah is for the interrogation of affirmation and reproach. The pronoun in "shara'ū" refers to the partners, and the pronoun in "lahum" refers to the disbelievers, though it was also said the reverse, and the first is preferred.

The meaning of ﴿what Allah did not permit﴾ is what He did not permit of polytheism and sins. ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, which is the delay of their punishment, as in His words, ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿it would have been judged between them﴾ in this world, and they would have been hastened to punishment. The pronoun in "baynahum" refers either to the believers and the polytheists, or to the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers, for them is a painful punishment﴾, that is, the polytheists and the deniers, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

The majority read "wa-inna al-ẓālimīna" with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf, beginning a new clause). Muslim, al-A'raj and Ibn Hurmuz read it with a fatḥah on it, as a conjunction over "kalimat al-faṣl" (the decisive word).

﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned﴾, that is: frightened and apprehensive of the evil deeds they earned, and that fear and apprehension will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And it will befall them﴾: the pronoun refers to "what they earned" with an elided noun in the construction, as al-Zajjaj said, that is: the recompense of what they earned will befall them and descend upon them without doubt, whether they feared it or not. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

Having mentioned the state of the wrongdoers, He mentioned the state of the believers, saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, in the meadows of the gardens﴾. Rawḍāt is the plural of rawḍah.

Abu Hayyan said: the common dialect is to pronounce the waw with a sukūn, while the dialect of Hudhayl pronounces it with a fatḥah. The rawḍah is a pleasant place abundant in greenery, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surah al-Rum. The rawḍah of Paradise is the finest of its dwellings, just as in this world it is the best of places. ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾ of kinds of blessings and types of delights. The governing element of "ʿinda rabbihim" is "yashāʾūna," or the governing element of "rawḍāt al-jannāt" is the stability (al-istiqrār). The indication by His words, "that" (dhālika), refers to what was mentioned before for the believers, and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it, which is ﴿It is the great bounty﴾, that is, one that cannot be described and that minds cannot reach in knowing its reality.

The indication by His words, ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants﴾, refers to the great bounty, that is: He gives them the good news of it.

Then He described the servants by His words, ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. These are the ones who combine faith and action in accordance with what Allah commanded and abstaining from what He forbade, and they are the ones given that good news.

The majority read "yubashshiru" with shaddah, from "bashsharа". Mujahid and Humayd ibn Qays read it with a ḍammah on the initial letter, a sukūn on the bā', and a kasrah on the shīn, from "abshara". Some of the Seven read it with a fatḥah on the initial letter and a ḍammah on the shīn. The explanation of the readings for this word has already passed.

Then, when He, glorified be He, mentioned what He informed His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, of these noble rulings contained in His Book, He commanded him to inform them that he does not ask them for any reward for this conveyance. So He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is: say, O Muhammad: I do not seek from you any payment or benefit for conveying the message, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. This exception may be connected (muttaṣil), meaning: except that you love me for my kinship among you, or love the people of my kin. It may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).

Al-Zajjaj said: "illā al-mawaddah" is an exception that is not from the first, meaning: except that you love me for my kinship, so that you protect me. The address is to the Quraysh, and this is the view of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik and al-Sha'bi. The meaning, on the disconnected reading, is: I do not ask you any reward at all, but I ask you for affection in the kinship that is between me and you. Respect me in it and do not hasten against me; leave me and the people. This was also the view of Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others, and it is the established view from Ibn ʿAbbas, as will come.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: they are the family of Muhammad. What those who hold this view cited as evidence will come.

Al-Hasan and others said: the meaning of the verse is: except seeking the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and drawing near to Him through obedience to Him.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Dahhak: this verse is abrogated (mansukh, superseded by a later ruling) and was revealed only in Mecca, when the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace. So Allah commanded them to show love to him. When he migrated, the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, and Allah then revealed to him: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and He revealed to him: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47].

What will make the reward clear and the meaning of the verse manifest will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him therein good﴾. The root of qarf is earning. It is said: "Fulan yaqrifu li-ʿiyālihi," meaning he earns for his dependants, and iqtirāf is earning, derived from their saying "rajul qirfah," when a man is cunning.

The meaning is: whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him this good deed in goodness by multiplying its reward.

Muqatil said: the meaning is: whoever earns a single good deed, We increase for him therein goodness, multiplying the single one tenfold or more.

It was also said: what is meant by this good deed is the affection for the near of kin, but applying it to the general sense is preferred, and the affection for the near of kin enters under it as a primary inclusion. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾, that is: abundantly forgiving to the sinners, and abundantly appreciative to the obedient.

Qatadah said: "Forgiving of sins, Appreciative of good deeds." al-Suddi said: "Forgiving of the sins of the family of Muhammad."

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ Am here is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿah) one, meaning: rather, do they say that Muhammad has fabricated a lie against Allah, by claiming prophethood? The denial is for rebuke. The meaning of fabricating a lie is inventing it.

Then He, glorified be He, answered their saying, saying: ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal over your heart﴾, that is: if he had fabricated a lie against Allah, He would have willed that it not come forth from him, and would have sealed upon his heart so that nothing of what he lied about would occur to his mind, as you claim.

Qatadah said: "He would seal over your heart, so He would make you forget the Qur'an." So He informed them that if he had fabricated against Him, He would have done to him what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said: "If He wills, He would bind your heart with patience regarding their harm, so that no hardship from their words enters your heart." It was also said: the address is to him, and what is meant is the disbelievers, that is: if He wills, He would seal the hearts of the disbelievers and hasten punishment upon them. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

It was also said: the meaning is: if your self had suggested to you to fabricate a lie against Allah, He would have sealed your heart, for no one dares to lie except one whose heart is sealed. The first view is preferred.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf) that confirms what precedes it of the denial of fabrication. Ibn al-Anbari said: "yakhtim ʿalā qalbika" is a complete clause, meaning that what follows is a new sentence. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in it, that is: and Allah erases falsehood. Al-Zajjaj said: "Am yaqūlūna iftarā ʿalā Allāhi kadhiban" is a complete clause.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are an argument against those who deny what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought, meaning: if what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought were false, He would have erased it, as His custom has been with fabricators. ﴿And establishes the truth through His words﴾, that is, Islam, and He makes it clear by His words, that is, by what He revealed of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, aware of what is in the hearts of the servants. The waw in "wa-yamḥu" was dropped in some copies of the Qur'an, as al-Kisa'i related.

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, that is: He accepts from the sinners among His servants their repentance to Him for the sins they committed and the evil deeds they earned. Repentance (tawbah) is regret over disobedience, with resolve not to return to it. It was also said: He accepts repentance from His friends and the people of His obedience. The first is preferred, for repentance is accepted from all servants, Muslim and disbeliever alike (p-1328), when it is sound, proceeding from sincerity of intention and sound resolve. ﴿And pardons evil deeds﴾ in general, for whoever repents of his evil deed. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾, of good and evil, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves.

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read "tafʿalūna" with the second person (taʾ) as address. The rest read it with the third person (yāʾ) as narration. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred the second reading, because this verb falls between two statements.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, He responds to them﴾. The relative pronoun is in the accusative position: Allah responds to those who believed and gives them what they asked of Him. It is said: "ajāba" and "istajāba" have the same meaning.

It was said: the meaning is that He accepts the worship of the sincere. It was also said that the implied sense is: "wa-yastajību lahum," so the lām was dropped, as it was dropped in His words, ﴿And when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3], meaning "kālū lahum" (they measured for them). It was also said that the relative pronoun is in the nominative position, meaning: they respond to their Lord when He calls them, as in His words, ﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of ﴿And those who believe respond﴾ is that those who believe seek a response; this is the true sense of the form istafʿala, so "alladhīna" is in the nominative position. The first is preferred.

﴿And He increases them from His bounty﴾, that is: He increases them beyond what they asked of Him, or beyond the reward they deserve, as a favour from Him. It was also said: He will grant them intercession for their brethren.

﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. This is for the disbelievers, in contrast to what He mentioned for the believers before it.

﴿And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would surely transgress in the earth﴾, that is: if Allah were to widen their provision, they would transgress in the earth, disobeying in it, being insolent toward the blessing, becoming arrogant, and seeking what is not theirs to seek. It was also said: the meaning is that if He made them equal in provision, some of them would not submit to others, and the crafts would cease. The first is preferred.

The apparent meaning is that it covers all kinds of provision. It has also been said that it refers specifically to rain. ﴿But He sends down in due measure what He wills.﴾ That is, He sends down provision to His servants in a measure according to His will and what His perfect wisdom requires. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing﴾ of their conditions, and sees what is good for them, whether in expanding or restricting provision. So He decrees for each one of them what suits him and restrains him from corruption through transgression on the earth.

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾ that is, the rain, which is the most beneficial kind of provision, the most widely useful, and the most productive of good. ﴿after they have despaired﴾ that is, after they have lost hope of it. Through this sending down of rain after despair, they will recognize the measure of His mercy toward them, and they will thank Him as thanks is due. ﴿And He is the Protecting Friend﴾ of His righteous servants, by doing good to them, bringing them benefits, and warding off harm from them, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, who deserves praise from them for His favors, both particular and general.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, that he said: "The life of the Hereafter." ﴿We will increase him in his tilth. And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "Whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter, Allah will not give him any share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will gain nothing from the world beyond provision that has already been finished and allotted to him."

Ahmad and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Hibban narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give good news to this Ummah of elevation, high standing, victory, and establishment in the land, so long as they do not seek the world through the deeds of the Hereafter. Whoever among them does the deeds of the Hereafter for the sake of this world, he will have no share in the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse, and then said: 'Allah says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your heart with richness and close off your poverty. If you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and will not close off your poverty.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ali, who said: "Tilth is of two kinds: the tilth of this world, which is wealth and children, and the tilth of the Hereafter, which is the lasting good deeds."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Tawus, from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about His saying ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The near of kin of the family of Muhammad." Ibn Abbas said: "I hasten to note that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the sake of my kinship, and that you protect the kinship that is between me and you."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from al-Sha'bi, who said: "People argued much about us concerning this verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾. So we wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about it, and he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the central link of lineage in Quraysh; there was no clan among its clans except that he had kinship with it. So Allah said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, that you love me because of your kinship with me, and that you protect me through it.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had kinship with all of Quraysh. When they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, he said: 'O people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then protect my kinship with you, and let no one other than you among the Arabs be more worthy of guarding and supporting me than you.'" Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him something similar. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him something similar. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, through another route, something similar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Ansar said: 'We did this and we did that,' and it seemed they were boasting. Al-Abbas said: 'We have superiority over you.' This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he came to them in their gatherings and said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humbled, and did Allah not honor you?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Will you not answer?' They said: 'What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Will you not say: Did your people not expel you, and we sheltered you? Did they not deny you, and we affirmed you? Did they not forsake you, and we supported you?' He kept saying this until they knelt on their knees and said: 'Our wealth and what is in our hands belong to Allah and His Messenger.' Then this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾." In its chain is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who is weak. The more likely view is that the verse is Meccan, not Medinan. We have already pointed out at the beginning of the surah the view of those who said that this verse and what follows it are Medinan, and this is their evidence.

Abu Nu'aym and al-Daylami narrated through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, that is: you protect me concerning my family and love them because of me."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated. al-Suyuti said, with a weak chain, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for the near of kin﴾, they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us?' He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists would love the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed, saying to them, O Muhammad: ﴿I do not ask you for it﴾, meaning, for what I call you to, ﴿any reward of a worldly kind﴾, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾, except that you protect me concerning my kinship with you. When he migrated to Medina, he wanted to join him with his brothers among the prophets, so he said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47], meaning: His reward and His honor in the Hereafter, as Noah said: ﴿I ask you for no reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and as Hud, Salih, and Shu'ayb said. They did not make an exception for a reward as the Prophet (ﷺ) did, so it was rejected from them. And this verse is abrogated."

Ahmad, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the verse: "Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience."

This is the summary of what has been transmitted from the scholar of the Ummah, Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the interpretation of this verse.

The first meaning is the one that is authentically reported from him, and it was narrated from him by a great number of his students and those after them. The report of abrogation transmitted from him does not contradict this. There is no obstacle to the Qur'an having been revealed in Mecca while the Quraysh disbelievers loved him because of the kinship between him and them, and protected him through it. Then that was abrogated, and this exception was removed from its origin, as indicated by what we have mentioned that shows he did not ask any reward at all for conveying the message. The view transmitted about interpreting it as referring to the family of Muhammad (ﷺ) is not strong enough to oppose the many reliable routes authentically reported from Ibn Abbas. Allah has indeed made the family of Muhammad independent of this through their noble virtues and beautiful qualities, and we have explained some of that when commenting on His saying: ﴿Allah only wants to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. Just as this view cannot withstand opposition, so too the report from him that the meaning of "affection in the near of kin" is that they love Allah and draw near to Him through His obedience is not strong enough. However, what strengthens this view is that it is a tafsir traced back (marfu') to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Its chain in Ahmad's Musnad is as follows: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said it, and he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Qaza'ah, with this same chain.

Ibn al-Mubarak, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated.

al-Suyuti said, with a sound chain, from Abu Hani' al-Khawlani, who said: "I heard Umar ibn Huraith and others saying: This verse was only revealed concerning the Companions of the Suffah: ﴿Had Allah expanded provision for His servants, they would have transgressed upon the earth﴾. That is because they said: 'If only we had...', and they wished for the world."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Ali something similar.

The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 42, verses 19–28 (part 1 of 2):

His words, ﴿Allah is Subtly Kind (latif) to His servants﴾: that is, He is greatly kind to them and extremely compassionate toward them.

Muqatil said: "Latif toward the righteous and the wicked, in that He does not kill them with hunger because of their sins." Ikrimah said: "Bārr (kind) toward them." Al-Suddi said: "Rafiq (gentle) toward them." It was also said: "Ḥafiyy (solicitous) toward them." Al-Qurtubi said: "Latif toward them in the presentation (of deeds) and in the reckoning," and other things have been said.

The meaning is that He extends His kindness to His servants in all their affairs, and among that is the provision (rizq) by which they live in this world. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾ from among them, however He wills. So He widens it for one and restricts it for another. ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, the Mighty in power, the Overpowering, the Capable, the Dominant who overcomes everything and is not overcome by anything.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth (ḥarth) of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾. Ḥarth in the language means earning. It is said: "He tills (yaḥruthu) for his dependants," and "yaḥtarith," meaning he earns. From this, a man is named Ḥārith. The original meaning of ḥarth is casting seed into the earth, and it was then applied, by way of metaphor (istiʿārah), to the fruits and benefits of deeds. The meaning is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of the Hereafter, Allah multiplies that for him, a good deed being rewarded tenfold up to seven hundred times over.

It was also said: its meaning is that He increases his success, his help, and the facilitation of the paths of good for him. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it﴾, that is: whoever, by his deeds and earning, desires the reward of this world, which is its enjoyment, and what Allah provides His servants from it, We give him from it what Our will decrees and what is apportioned to him in Our decree.

Qatadah said: the meaning of ﴿We give him from it﴾ is: We ordain for him what has been apportioned to him, as in His words, ﴿We hasten for him therein what We will﴾ [al-Isra': 18]. Qatadah also said: Allah gives, out of the intention of the Hereafter, whatever of worldly affairs He wills, but He gives out of the intention of this world only the world. Al-Qushayri said: the apparent meaning is that the verse concerns the disbeliever, but this is a specification without a specifier (takhsīs bi-ghayr mukhassis).

Then He, glorified be He, explained that this one who intends the world by his deeds has no share in the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And he has no share in the Hereafter﴾, because he did not work for the Hereafter, so there is no share for him in it. The interpretation of this verse has already been given in Surah al-Isra'.

﴿Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah did not permit?﴾ When He, glorified be He, had explained the principle regarding the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, He followed it with an explanation of the great sin that necessitates the Fire. The hamzah is for the interrogation of affirmation and reproach. The pronoun in "shara'ū" refers to the partners, and the pronoun in "lahum" refers to the disbelievers, though it was also said the reverse, and the first is preferred.

The meaning of ﴿what Allah did not permit﴾ is what He did not permit of polytheism and sins. ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, which is the delay of their punishment, as in His words, ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿it would have been judged between them﴾ in this world, and they would have been hastened to punishment. The pronoun in "baynahum" refers either to the believers and the polytheists, or to the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers, for them is a painful punishment﴾, that is, the polytheists and the deniers, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

The majority read "wa-inna al-ẓālimīna" with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf, beginning a new clause). Muslim, al-A'raj and Ibn Hurmuz read it with a fatḥah on it, as a conjunction over "kalimat al-faṣl" (the decisive word).

﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned﴾, that is: frightened and apprehensive of the evil deeds they earned, and that fear and apprehension will be on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And it will befall them﴾: the pronoun refers to "what they earned" with an elided noun in the construction, as al-Zajjaj said, that is: the recompense of what they earned will befall them and descend upon them without doubt, whether they feared it or not. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl).

Having mentioned the state of the wrongdoers, He mentioned the state of the believers, saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, in the meadows of the gardens﴾. Rawḍāt is the plural of rawḍah.

Abu Hayyan said: the common dialect is to pronounce the waw with a sukūn, while the dialect of Hudhayl pronounces it with a fatḥah. The rawḍah is a pleasant place abundant in greenery, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surah al-Rum. The rawḍah of Paradise is the finest of its dwellings, just as in this world it is the best of places. ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾ of kinds of blessings and types of delights. The governing element of "ʿinda rabbihim" is "yashāʾūna," or the governing element of "rawḍāt al-jannāt" is the stability (al-istiqrār). The indication by His words, "that" (dhālika), refers to what was mentioned before for the believers, and its predicate is the sentence mentioned after it, which is ﴿It is the great bounty﴾, that is, one that cannot be described and that minds cannot reach in knowing its reality.

The indication by His words, ﴿That is what Allah gives good news of to His servants﴾, refers to the great bounty, that is: He gives them the good news of it.

Then He described the servants by His words, ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. These are the ones who combine faith and action in accordance with what Allah commanded and abstaining from what He forbade, and they are the ones given that good news.

The majority read "yubashshiru" with shaddah, from "bashsharа". Mujahid and Humayd ibn Qays read it with a ḍammah on the initial letter, a sukūn on the bā', and a kasrah on the shīn, from "abshara". Some of the Seven read it with a fatḥah on the initial letter and a ḍammah on the shīn. The explanation of the readings for this word has already passed.

Then, when He, glorified be He, mentioned what He informed His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, of these noble rulings contained in His Book, He commanded him to inform them that he does not ask them for any reward for this conveyance. So He said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is: say, O Muhammad: I do not seek from you any payment or benefit for conveying the message, ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. This exception may be connected (muttaṣil), meaning: except that you love me for my kinship among you, or love the people of my kin. It may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).

Al-Zajjaj said: "illā al-mawaddah" is an exception that is not from the first, meaning: except that you love me for my kinship, so that you protect me. The address is to the Quraysh, and this is the view of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik and al-Sha'bi. The meaning, on the disconnected reading, is: I do not ask you any reward at all, but I ask you for affection in the kinship that is between me and you. Respect me in it and do not hasten against me; leave me and the people. This was also the view of Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and others, and it is the established view from Ibn ʿAbbas, as will come.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: they are the family of Muhammad. What those who hold this view cited as evidence will come.

Al-Hasan and others said: the meaning of the verse is: except seeking the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and drawing near to Him through obedience to Him.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Dahhak: this verse is abrogated (mansukh, superseded by a later ruling) and was revealed only in Mecca, when the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace. So Allah commanded them to show love to him. When he migrated, the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, and Allah then revealed to him: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109], and He revealed to him: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves; my reward is only from Allah﴾ [Saba': 47].

What will make the reward clear and the meaning of the verse manifest will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills.

﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him therein good﴾. The root of qarf is earning. It is said: "Fulan yaqrifu li-ʿiyālihi," meaning he earns for his dependants, and iqtirāf is earning, derived from their saying "rajul qirfah," when a man is cunning.

The meaning is: whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him this good deed in goodness by multiplying its reward.

Muqatil said: the meaning is: whoever earns a single good deed, We increase for him therein goodness, multiplying the single one tenfold or more.

It was also said: what is meant by this good deed is the affection for the near of kin, but applying it to the general sense is preferred, and the affection for the near of kin enters under it as a primary inclusion. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾, that is: abundantly forgiving to the sinners, and abundantly appreciative to the obedient.

Qatadah said: "Forgiving of sins, Appreciative of good deeds." al-Suddi said: "Forgiving of the sins of the family of Muhammad."

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ Am here is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿah) one, meaning: rather, do they say that Muhammad has fabricated a lie against Allah, by claiming prophethood? The denial is for rebuke. The meaning of fabricating a lie is inventing it.

Then He, glorified be He, answered their saying, saying: ﴿If Allah wills, He would seal over your heart﴾, that is: if he had fabricated a lie against Allah, He would have willed that it not come forth from him, and would have sealed upon his heart so that nothing of what he lied about would occur to his mind, as you claim.

Qatadah said: "He would seal over your heart, so He would make you forget the Qur'an." So He informed them that if he had fabricated against Him, He would have done to him what He informed them of in this verse. Mujahid and Muqatil said: "If He wills, He would bind your heart with patience regarding their harm, so that no hardship from their words enters your heart." It was also said: the address is to him, and what is meant is the disbelievers, that is: if He wills, He would seal the hearts of the disbelievers and hasten punishment upon them. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri.

It was also said: the meaning is: if your self had suggested to you to fabricate a lie against Allah, He would have sealed your heart, for no one dares to lie except one whose heart is sealed. The first view is preferred.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are a resumed sentence (istiʾnāf) that confirms what precedes it of the denial of fabrication. Ibn al-Anbari said: "yakhtim ʿalā qalbika" is a complete clause, meaning that what follows is a new sentence. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in it, that is: and Allah erases falsehood. Al-Zajjaj said: "Am yaqūlūna iftarā ʿalā Allāhi kadhiban" is a complete clause.

His words, ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾, are an argument against those who deny what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought, meaning: if what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, brought were false, He would have erased it, as His custom has been with fabricators. ﴿And establishes the truth through His words﴾, that is, Islam, and He makes it clear by His words, that is, by what He revealed of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, aware of what is in the hearts of the servants. The waw in "wa-yamḥu" was dropped in some copies of the Qur'an, as al-Kisa'i related.

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, that is: He accepts from the sinners among His servants their repentance to Him for the sins they committed and the evil deeds they earned. Repentance (tawbah) is regret over disobedience, with resolve not to return to it. It was also said: He accepts repentance from His friends and the people of His obedience. The first is preferred, for repentance is accepted from all servants, Muslim and disbeliever alike (p-1328), when it is sound, proceeding from sincerity of intention and sound resolve. ﴿And pardons evil deeds﴾ in general, for whoever repents of his evil deed. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾, of good and evil, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves.

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read "tafʿalūna" with the second person (taʾ) as address. The rest read it with the third person (yāʾ) as narration. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim preferred the second reading, because this verb falls between two statements.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, He responds to them﴾. The relative pronoun is in the accusative position: Allah responds to those who believed and gives them what they asked of Him. It is said: "ajāba" and "istajāba" have the same meaning.

It was said: the meaning is that He accepts the worship of the sincere. It was also said that the implied sense is: "wa-yastajību lahum," so the lām was dropped, as it was dropped in His words, ﴿And when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3], meaning "kālū lahum" (they measured for them). It was also said that the relative pronoun is in the nominative position, meaning: they respond to their Lord when He calls them, as in His words, ﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. Al-Mubarrad said: the meaning of ﴿And those who believe respond﴾ is that those who believe seek a response; this is the true sense of the form istafʿala, so "alladhīna" is in the nominative position. The first is preferred.

﴿And He increases them from His bounty﴾, that is: He increases them beyond what they asked of Him, or beyond the reward they deserve, as a favour from Him. It was also said: He will grant them intercession for their brethren.

﴿And the disbelievers, for them is a severe punishment﴾. This is for the disbelievers, in contrast to what He mentioned for the believers before it.

﴿And if Allah were to extend provision to His servants, they would surely transgress in the earth﴾, that is: if Allah were to widen their provision, they would transgress in the earth, disobeying in it, being insolent toward the blessing, becoming arrogant, and seeking what is not theirs to seek. It was also said: the meaning is that if He made them equal in provision, some of them would not submit to others, and the crafts would cease. The first is preferred.

The apparent meaning is that it covers all kinds of provision. It has also been said that it refers specifically to rain. ﴿But He sends down in due measure what He wills.﴾ That is, He sends down provision to His servants in a measure according to His will and what His perfect wisdom requires. ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with His servants and Seeing﴾ of their conditions, and sees what is good for them, whether in expanding or restricting provision. So He decrees for each one of them what suits him and restrains him from corruption through transgression on the earth.

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾ that is, the rain, which is the most beneficial kind of provision, the most widely useful, and the most productive of good. ﴿after they have despaired﴾ that is, after they have lost hope of it. Through this sending down of rain after despair, they will recognize the measure of His mercy toward them, and they will thank Him as thanks is due. ﴿And He is the Protecting Friend﴾ of His righteous servants, by doing good to them, bringing them benefits, and warding off harm from them, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, who deserves praise from them for His favors, both particular and general.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, that he said: "The life of the Hereafter." ﴿We will increase him in his tilth. And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: "Whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter, Allah will not give him any share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he will gain nothing from the world beyond provision that has already been finished and allotted to him."

Ahmad and al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Hibban narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give good news to this Ummah of elevation, high standing, victory, and establishment in the land, so long as they do not seek the world through the deeds of the Hereafter. Whoever among them does the deeds of the Hereafter for the sake of this world, he will have no share in the Hereafter."

al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse, and then said: 'Allah says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your heart with richness and close off your poverty. If you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and will not close off your poverty.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Asakir narrated from Ali, who said: "Tilth is of two kinds: the tilth of this world, which is wealth and children, and the tilth of the Hereafter, which is the lasting good deeds."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Tawus, from Ibn Abbas that he was asked about His saying ﴿except affection for the near of kin﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The near of kin of the family of Muhammad." Ibn Abbas said: "I hasten to note that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no clan of Quraysh except that he had kinship with them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the sake of my kinship, and that you protect the kinship that is between me and you."
